title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine months | Niger | The Guardian
description: Kevin Rideout, who was abducted by unknown assailants in Niamey, said to be in good health and in care of US officials
Author: Eromo Egbejule
Headline: Kevin Rideout, who was abducted by unknown assailants in Niamey, said to be in good health and in care of US officials
Content: Soldiers on patrol in Niamey. Kevin Rideout was kidnapped in Niger’s capital and no armed group claimed responsibility for the abduction.Photograph: Issouf Sanogo/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSoldiers on patrol in Niamey. Kevin Rideout was kidnapped in Niger’s capital and no armed group claimed responsibility for the abduction.Photograph: Issouf Sanogo/AFP/Getty ImagesNigerAmerican missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine monthsKevin Rideout, who was abducted by unknown assailants in Niamey, said to be in good health and in care of US officialsEromo Egbejulein Abidjan and agenciesFri 14 Aug 2026 10.55 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 05.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn American missionary who was kidnapped inNigerin October has been released, his organisation has said.Serving in Mission International saidKevin Rideout “is in good health in the care of US officials” and would soon be reunited with his extended family.Donald Trump, who claimed to have helped secure Rideout’s release, later said he was “back in United States Custody” on Friday.The 50-year-old missionary pilot was kidnapped in the west African country’s capital, Niamey, on 21 October by three armed individuals and was probably driven out of town, according to a security official at the time. No armed group claimed responsibility for the abduction. Other details about his rescue remain unknown.The US president’s administration had made the release of Rideout a priority in its latest strategy on AfricanSahelstates, after years of fighting extremism found limited success. Rideout had been working in Niger for 19 years as a missionary before the incident.View image in fullscreenThe American missionary Kevin Rideout is said to now be in safe hands.Photograph: Hostage Aid Worldwide“I am proud to announce that Kevin Rideout, a wonderful Christian Missionary, is back in United States Custody,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform on Friday. “Kevin, the United States of America looks forward to welcoming you HOME. Glad to have helped!”Niger has long been the target of attacks by armed groups, including jihadis linked to al-Qaida and Islamic State. A “continually deteriorating security situation” across the country was cited by the military juntathat took power in 2023when deposing the democratically elected president, Mohamed Bazoum.The new authorities ousted western partners, including the US, which had soldiers in Niger, andforged a new security and diplomatic alliancewith Russia. One former US base has since been occupied by Russian soldiers.How rampant violence made Nigeria an insecurity hotspot in the Sahel – mappedRead moreTrump described the broader region of west Africa as “the epicenter of Islamist terrorism” in his social media post on Friday, claiming there had been “more deadly attacks in the past year” there than anywhere else on Earth.Washington has since shifted its focus to coastal west African states including Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana, sharing intelligence with local security personnel to prevent extremist threats from spilling southwards from the arid Sahel.However, the insurgency continues to escalate in the region. In Niger, data from Acled, the armed conflict data aggregator, shows that civilian fatalities rose by nearly 50% in the year after Bazoum was ousted.Cities and urban centres in the Sahel region have also been increasingly targeted by armed non-state actors as the crisis reaches new dimensions.The US embassy in Niamey issued a security alert a day after Rideout’s abduction, warning that American citizens “remain at a heightened risk of kidnapping throughout Niger, including in the capital city”.In June, more than 30 people were killed when gunmen attacked the main airport in Niamey. It wasthe second attack this year at the airport, a strategic hub that serves as the ruling military’s command, hosting its air force base and most of its drones and aircraft. It is also the headquarters of the Alliance of Sahel States, the regional alliance that brings together troops from Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso.In April, Mali’sdefence minister, Gen Sadio Camara, was killedin his home on the outskirts of the capital Bamako during coordinated assaults staged by insurgents including the west African affiliate of al-Qaida.Associated Press and Agence France-Presse contributedreportingExplore more on these topicsNigerAfricaSahelMaliAl-QaidaUS foreign policynewsShareReuse this content

title: Ontario free to axe Toronto bike lanes, region’s top court rules | Toronto | The Guardian
description: Win is significant for region’s premier, Doug Ford, who blames protected zones for city’s traffic ills
Author: Olivia Bowden
Headline: Win is significant for region’s premier, Doug Ford, who blames protected zones for city’s traffic ills
Content: A bike lane in downtown Toronto. It’s been estimated that ripping up the lanes would cost taxpayers C$48m.Photograph: Andrew Francis Wallace/Toronto Star/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA bike lane in downtown Toronto. It’s been estimated that ripping up the lanes would cost taxpayers C$48m.Photograph: Andrew Francis Wallace/Toronto Star/Getty ImagesTorontoOntario free to axe Toronto bike lanes, region’s top court rulesWin is significant for region’s premier, Doug Ford, who blames protected zones for city’s traffic illsOlivia BowdenFri 14 Aug 2026 17.03 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 17.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Ontario government is now free to rip out Toronto’s bike lanes on its busiest streets after the region’s top court ruled in favour of the province on Friday, overturning a lower court’s decision that decreed removal would violate constitutional rights.The win is significant for Ontario’s premier, Doug Ford, and his government, who have long railed against Toronto’s bike lanes, blaming the protected zones forthe city’s traffic ills.In 2024, the Ford government passed legislation that would allow Ontario to axe Toronto’s lanes, despite the recent installation of the infrastructure by the municipality.But the effort to tear up the lanes covering 19km (12 miles) of road was paused after cycling advocacy organisations levelled a legal challenge against the province.Their challenge was supported in July 2025, when a superior court judge ruled removing the lanes was unconstitutional, as it would create a heightened risk of death or injury, in turn violating the right to life and security of the person. Those rights are protected under Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.Friday’s decision from the Ontario court of appeal reverses that ruling. Michael Longfield, executive director of Cycle Toronto, one of the groups that launched the legal challenge, said he is disappointed in the decision.“This isn’t just about keeping people on bikes safe. It helps pedestrians. It helps other drivers. It has a very strong traffic calming effect that we need in major cities,” he said.The court of appeal judges in their decision wrote that there is no charter right to bike lanes and the government is free to change legislation on the lanes if it wishes. They explained that courts cannot find legislation unconstitutional because experts predict the government’s policies will fail.“Neither the government nor the legislature is under any obligation to accept policy advice,” wrote Justice Huscroft in the decision.In reaction to the ruling, Toronto’s mayor, Olivia Chow, said she has been working with the province to negotiate a path forward “that keeps every road user safe”. There’s hope the municipality will negotiate an alternative with the Ford government that still makes room for cyclists, said Longfield.Ontario’s transportation minister, Prabmeet Sarkaria, said in a statement the top court’s decision is a “victory for common sense”. The government has not yet announced when or if they plan to remove the lanes.It was estimated by a city report in 2024 that ripping up the lanes would cost taxpayers an additional C$48m (£26m). Internal briefings obtainedby the Trilliumalso found the province’s own staff reported that bike lane removal would not reduce congestion and could make it worse. Those staff members also warned Ontario may be seen as encroaching on municipal decision-making.Fundamentally, Ford targeting bike lanes is a gross overreach of the provincial government into city affairs, said Longfield. It is “frankly ridiculous”, he said, to believe the key to solving urban congestion is barring bike lanes.“The more we can focus on real, evidence-based solutions … the better it will be,” he said.Explore more on these topicsTorontoCanadaCyclingAmericasnewsShareReuse this content

title: Canadian plasma clinics pause collections after deaths of two donors | Canada | The Guardian
description: Grifols, which runs private chain of clinics, to temporarily stop taking donations after new government investigation
Author: Olivia Bowden
Headline: Grifols, which runs private chain of clinics, to temporarily stop taking donations after new government investigation
Content: An autopsy showed Rodiyat Alabede, 22, died of cardiac arrest shortly after donating plasma in Winnipeg in 2025.Photograph: gofundmeAn autopsy showed Rodiyat Alabede, 22, died of cardiac arrest shortly after donating plasma in Winnipeg in 2025.Photograph: gofundmeCanadaCanadian plasma clinics pause collections after deaths of two donorsGrifols, which runs private chain of clinics, to temporarily stop taking donations after new government investigationOlivia Bowdenin TorontoFri 14 Aug 2026 12.21 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 13.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA chain of private plasma donation clinics inCanadahas said it is pausing collections after the deaths of two donors and a new government investigation into potential unsafe practices.Grifols, a Spanish healthcare company which runs 17 clinics in Canada and is the country’s only private clinic for plasma donation, said it informedHealthCanada of its decision to temporarily pause collections on Wednesday.On the same day, the agency had issued a formal notice of non-compliance for failure to follow blood regulations, a senior officialtold the Globe and Mail newspaper.The two deaths occurred after plasma donations in October 2025 and January 2026,Health Canada said in March of this year. The donors, both of whom were in the province of Manitoba, went into “distress” while donating, people familiar with the cases said.Though Health Canada did not release the identities of the donors, friends said one was Rodiyat Alabede, 22, an international student and aspiring social worker who donated plasma in Winnipeg on 25 October.Patientadvocates reported at the end of Maythat there were concerns about whether Alabede had been properly screened.“They had staff taking plasma from donors who did not know how to extract plasma in a safe manner,” alleged Kat Lanteigne, a safe blood campaigner who represents Alabede’s family.“The [failures] were so egregious that … now we have more questions than answers,” she said in May.An autopsy showed Alabede died of cardiac arrest shortly after donating. Health Canada reported that it found “no link” between Alabede’s death and plasma donation.Patient advocates have called for a new inquest into her death, however, after alleging that “significant medical discrepancies” had been uncovered between her autopsy, which was completed two days after her death, and the medical summary drafted by Health Canada published on 27 March of this year.The Guardian has also seen Health Canada inspection reports from May that found deficiencies at Grifols clinics, including inadequate training for staff, failures in standard operating procedures, poor record-keeping and a failure by Grifols to remedy past issues.The Health Canada report also found that staff did not stop plasma collection when alarms went off, and described the company’s reporting as “incomplete” and “inaccurate”.Prior to the newly announced pause, donations were permitted at Grifols twice a week. The company paid donors up to C$100 (£55) for each donation.Plasma is a pale yellow, protein-rich liquid in blood that assists in moving red and white blood cells, along with platelets, through blood vessels, according to Canadian Blood Services, the non-profit that operates Canada’s national blood supply.Plasma also helps prevent excessive bleeding and is used to create medications for a variety of conditions including haemophilia, liver disease and various cancers.The plasma donation process differs from donating blood overall. A medical device called an apheresis machine draws the blood, separates it into individual parts, collects the components needed and then returns the remaining blood back into the body, according to Canadian Blood Services. The process takes about 90 minutes, whereas a general blood draw takes about 10.In Canada, provinces and territories decide whether paid plasma clinics are permitted. British Columbia and Quebec do not allow the practice, for example, but Manitoba, where the deaths occurred, does not prohibit companies from paying donors for plasma.Grifols said it decided to pause collection “proactively and voluntarily” due to what it deemed “unfounded attention”. It said the pause would allow it to work with Health Canada and Canadian Blood Services.The company has denied the two deaths were connected to plasma donation.On Friday, Health Canada said it found “various deficiencies” specifically at the Taylor Avenue Grifols location in Winnipeg. A spokesperson for that location said it was working closely with the company so that it could return to operations.“Canadians can be assured that this decision will have no impact on the safety and security of Canada’s blood and plasma supply,” Grifols said.Explore more on these topicsCanadaHealthAmericasnewsShareReuse this content

title: BP to develop offshore gasfield in Venezuela with firms linked to Trump administration | BP | The Guardian
description: Move will be one of first large-scale foreign investments in country since US ousted leader Nicolás Maduro in January
Author: Jillian Ambrose
Headline: Move will be one of first large-scale foreign investments in country since US ousted leader Nicolás Maduro in January
Content: BP’s decision comes after Donald Trump called for foreign oil companies to invest ‘at least $100bn’ to help rebuild and tap Venezuela’s resources.Photograph: Arnd Wiegmann/ReutersView image in fullscreenBP’s decision comes after Donald Trump called for foreign oil companies to invest ‘at least $100bn’ to help rebuild and tap Venezuela’s resources.Photograph: Arnd Wiegmann/ReutersBPBP to develop offshore gasfield in Venezuela with firms linked to Trump administrationMove will be one of first large-scale foreign investments in country since US ousted leader Nicolás Maduro in JanuaryJillian AmbroseEnergy correspondentFri 14 Aug 2026 10.04 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 14.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBP has answered Donald Trump’s call for oil companies to help rebuild Venezuela’s fossil fuel industry with new plans to develop a large offshore gasfield.BP will partner with two oil firms with close links to the Trump administration to develop the second phase of the Loran gasfield, in one of the first large-scale foreign investments in Venezuela since theUS ousted its leader Nicolás Maduroin January.The London-listed oil company holds a licence to develop the field alongside a Qatari company owned by the Al-Khayyat brothers, the Syrian-born billionaires working with Ivanka Trump, the US president’s daughter, and her husband, Jared Kushner, to build a controversialmultibillion-dollar resort in Albania.BP will also work alongside the overseas investment arm of UAE’s national oil company run by the industry minister, Sultan Al Jaber, who in 2025 promised Trump that the Gulf state would increase its investments in the US energy sector more than sixfold to $440bn (£325bn) within a decade.The deal makes BP one of the first large-scale international oil firms to return toVenezuelaafter rival Shell secured a licence to develop the first phase of the Loran field earlier this summer. Caracas is also in talks over oil projects with the Italian oil company Eni.Meg O’Neill, BP’s chief executive, described the licence as “an important step forward” in the company’s collaboration with Caracas, which “reflects the progress we have made together”.BP is one of a handful of European oil firms that have returned to the basin since Trump called for foreign oil companies to invest “at least $100bn” to helprebuild and tap Venezuela’s oil resourcesafter capturing the country’s former president.The US oil companies ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips have begun scouting opportunities in Venezuela, but have been slower to play a role in its fossil fuel revival after the Latin American country nationalised the industry in 2007. Chevron remained in the country as a minority partner to Venezuela’s state oil company and has continued to produce crude.BP’s licence was awarded almost four months after it agreed to work with the Venezuelan government to explore potential gas development. It was also one of the first big agreements struck by O’Neill, a US-born former ExxonMobil executive, in her first month at the helm.O’Neill said: “BP has a longstanding presence in the region and deep experience developing major gas resources. Together, these agreements provide a strong foundation to progress Venezuela’s offshore gas potential and unlock the next phase of development.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionVenezuela is believed to have thelargest oil reserves of any country in the world, and in the late 1990s produced more than 3.5m barrels of a oil a day as one of the top 10 crude producers in the world. However, a quarter of a century of neglect, underinvestment and corruption have eroded its oil industry and caused output to fall to roughly 1m barrels a day.In the months since theTrump administrationseized control of Venezuela’s oil industry, oil output has climbed to 1.2m barrels a day, allowing exports to US refineries to reach their highest level since 2019.Explore more on these topicsBPVenezuelaGasOil and gas companiesEnergy industryDonald TrumpAmericasnewsShareReuse this content

title: Strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes eastern Indonesia, killing two  | Indonesia | The Guardian
description: Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground
Content: Strong earthquake hits IndonesiaIndonesiaStrong 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes eastern Indonesia, killing twoShallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher groundGuardian staff and agenciesFri 14 Aug 2026 19.43 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 22.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck easternIndonesiaearly on Saturday, killing two people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly earthquakes.Authorities initially issued a tsunami warning, but it has since been lifted.The shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region with a depth of 10km at 5.58am local time, according to the US Geological Survey, followed by two aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1.“At this point there are two reported fatalities” – a man and a woman, disaster agency spokesperson Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan told reporters in Jakarta, adding that authorities were still determining the full extent of the damage.The epicentre of the quake was located off the north coast of Flores island, about 68km (42 miles) northwest of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said.Residents in Nagekeo regency, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground immediately after the earthquake.“Suddenly it started to shake and I panicked,” 31-year-old hospital customer service official, Lukas Lotar told AFP. “Patients also fled the hospital, the jolt was big. I saw some walls were cracked,” he added.View image in fullscreenPeople flee their homes to seek safety after a earthquake in Talibura Village, Sikka, East Nusa Tenggara on 15 August 2026.Photograph: Arnold Welianto/AFP/Getty ImagesNagekeo resident Yohanes Babo, 56, said he was at a market when the quake hit.“The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house,” he said.“People were panicking, running here and there. We’re evacuating for the time being … and trying to get to the hills,” he said, adding: “My family is safe. No one was harmed.”Authorities issued a tsunami warning but later lifted it when Indonesia’s meteorology, climatology and geophysics agency (BMKG) said monitoring showed no significant sea level changes that would pose a threat to coastal communities.“We have ended (the tsunami warning) but we will keep monitoring the sea level,” said BMKG earthquake and tsunami director Wijayanto.Images broadcast on Indonesian television showed hundreds of people in nearby Nagekeo regency evacuating the area surrounded by the rubble of damaged buildings.The quake was felt across much of Flores island with initial reports indicating heavy damage.Yohanna Embu, a resident of Sikka, a regency within East Nusa Tenggara province, said a number of buildings were damaged by the strong shaking and panicked people ran to higher ground.“Many buildings here were damaged … I saw that the waiting room at the port terminal in Maumere had collapsed,” she said.View image in fullscreenHouses were damaged by the 7.7-magnitude earthquake in Ruteng, Manggarai, East Nusa Tenggara, on 15 August 2026.Photograph: SELO/AFP/Getty ImagesIndonesia, a vast archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, is prone to earthquakes and volcanic activity because of its location on the “Ring of Fire”, an arc of volcanoes and fault lines in the Pacific Basin.Separately, Australia’s tsunami ⁠warning centre said the undersea earthquake ​will ​have “no tsunami ​threat to the Australian mainland, ​islands ‌or territories”.*With Agence France-Presse and ReutersExplore more on these topicsIndonesiaEarthquakesAsia PacificnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Unprecedented’ rain kills five in Japan as thousands stranded at airport | Japan | The Guardian
description: Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 after flooding, landslide warnings and power outages in Chiba prefecture
Author: Gavin Blair
Headline: Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 after flooding, landslide warnings and power outages in Chiba prefecture
Content: At least four killed as record rainfall floods Japan's Chiba prefecture – videoJapan‘Unprecedented’ rain kills five in Japan as thousands stranded at airportEvacuation orders issued for 400,000 after flooding, landslide warnings and power outages in Chiba prefectureGavin Blairin Tokyo and Lysia WrightFri 14 Aug 2026 09.11 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 00.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt least five people have died in easternJapanafter “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings.The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people in Chiba and other areas, and about 45,000 homes lost power, as 115mm of rain fell hourly, approximately the same amount usually recorded for the whole month of August.It was the first time the Japan Meteorological Agency has issued the highest level-5 warning for heavy rains and landslides for the prefecture.Potatoes ‘boil’ in the ground as record heatwave sweeps across swathes of AsiaRead moreThe body of a man, believed to be in his 60s or 70s, was found floating in a flooded road in the city of Ichikawa, while a 66-year-old woman was killed when her car got trapped in flood waters in the city of Sakura. Two other people are reported to have died after being unable to escape from their cars during the flooding. Soldiers have been dispatched to the area ‌to help with relief efforts.“This case was an extremely unusual situation,” Chiba governor Toshihito Kumagai told reporters on Friday morning. “I have responded to many disasters in the past, but I have never experienced a case like this.”View image in fullscreenA makeshift evacuation centre set up at the Chiba prefectural government building after transport was disrupted by the torrential rain.Photograph: Kyodo/ReutersApproximately 7,000 passengers spent the night at Narita, one of Tokyo’s main international airports, while 1,700 people sought shelter at the Chiba prefectural government building.Footage from public broadcaster NHK showed water spurting violently from what appeared to be a maintenance hole and exceeding the height of a nearby five-storey building in Chiba’s central ward.View image in fullscreenFlooded areas after heavy rain in Chiba prefecture.Photograph: Kyodo/ReutersA woman in Ichikawa told NHK the rain “happened all of a sudden so it was a complete surprise”.“The power is out so I’m worried whether I can open my business in the next couple of days,” she said.A traveller from the UK who gave his name as Philip told AFP that he had to go through a nine-hour journey, including a taxi ride, before finally arriving at the airport early on Friday morning.With a sleeping bag in hand, he said he has “just been trying to get some sleep and watching Netflix”.“Just get on with it, really. Nothing else you can do,” he said.Rain had eased by Friday but authorities are warning of the dangers of flooding in the area.“For rivers where the risk of flooding is already high, please take action to protect your lives in any way possible,” said Kazuhito Shimamoto of the ministry of land, infrastructure, transport and tourism.“There are also rivers where the risk of flooding is expected to increase further, so please check the evacuation advisories issued by your local municipalities and evacuate early.”Meteorologists in Japan say that climate breakdown is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events.Reuters and Agence France-Presse contributed to this reportExplore more on these topicsJapanAsia PacificExtreme weatherFloodingClimate crisisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Indonesia wildfires threaten orangutans rescued from animal traffickers | Indonesia | The Guardian
description: Blaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centre
Author: Jonathan Watts
Headline: Blaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centre
Content: Firefighters and staff from the centre battle to contain the approaching wildfire.Photograph: YiariView image in fullscreenFirefighters and staff from the centre battle to contain the approaching wildfire.Photograph: YiariIndonesiaIndonesia wildfires threaten orangutans rescued from animal traffickersBlaze fuelled by hot, dry and windy conditions comes within metres of West Kalimantan rehabilitation centreJonathan WattsFri 14 Aug 2026 00.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 00.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOrangutans rescued from wildlife traffickers face a new threat from the record number of fires that have broken out inIndonesiain recent weeks.Flames have come within metres of an animal rehabilitation centre in West Kalimantan as hot, dry and windy conditions have been amplified by a powerful El Niño and the human-driven climate crisis.In the first 13 days of August, Indonesia registered more than three times moreforest fire hotspotsthan in the whole of the same month last year. This followed a record number of blazes between January and July.West Kalimantan has been at the epicentre. After 40 days without rain, there have been dozens of severe outbreaks of fire in the region.View image in fullscreenOrangutans at the Yiari rehabilitation centre.Photograph: YiariFlames threatened theYiariorangutan rehabilitation centre this week. The fire moved rapidly from 1km away to within 100 metres of the perimeter within days, prompting staff to relocate the 60resident orangutansto enclosures in the middle of the centre.‘Should we leave them to die?’ The battle over how to save orangutans from the curse of palm oilRead moreIndonesia authorities have water-bombed the forest to try to control the blaze, and teams from the centre joined the firefighting efforts as the air quality worsened, posing a threat to animals and the wider ecosystem.The centre’s director, Dr Karmele Llano Sánchez, said in her latest update that battling the fire had been relentless. “We were fighting it until 3am, but this morning it has reignited. The teams are working round the clock but they are exhausted.”The situation had reportedly stabilised as of Thursday evening, with all the animals safe, but the meteorological agency has said the hot, dry conditions are likely to continue and could lead to more outbreaks.Indonesian authorities have urged people to avoid setting fires and to remain vigilant because the peak of the fire season is usually in September and October.Yiari is seeking funds for more firefighting equipment. Itwarnedof the growing threat earlier this year after a fire started for land clearing spread into one of its ecosystem restoration sites.Explore more on these topicsIndonesiaWildfiresConservationWildlifeAnimalsAsia PacificnewsShareReuse this content

title: French court blocks Macron’s social media ban for under-15s | Social media bans | The Guardian
description: Constitutional council says curbs infringe freedom of expression and privacy as president vows to rework legislation
Author: Dan Milmo
Headline: Constitutional council says curbs infringe freedom of expression and privacy as president vows to rework legislation
Content: The EU plans to seek stronger protections for children from harmful social media features.Photograph: Jeremy Piper/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe EU plans to seek stronger protections for children from harmful social media features.Photograph: Jeremy Piper/ReutersSocial media bansFrench court blocks Macron’s social media ban for under-15sConstitutional council says curbs infringe freedom of expression and privacy as president vows to rework legislationDan MilmoGlobal technology editorFri 14 Aug 2026 13.12 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 12.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFrance’s top court has blocked a ban on social media access for under-15s, ruling that it infringed freedom of expression and privacy.The decision is a blow to PresidentEmmanuel Macronas momentum builds around the world for Australian-style restrictions on children’s use of social media.A lawapproved by parliament in Julywould have barred under-15s from opening social media accounts from the beginning of September. Tech platforms would also have been required to close existing accounts within four months and use age-verification tools approved by ⁠France’s privacy regulator.However, the constitutional council found that while the law required users to provide proof ​of age, it failed to specify the “conditions and limits” ‌under which this should happen. It also found that the restrictions infringed freedom of expression and privacy.“The council holds that the contested provisions, on ‌the one hand, disproportionately infringe upon the freedom of expression and communication and, on the other, fail to provide the legal safeguards necessary to ensure the right to respect for private life,” it said.Several countries havefollowed the example of Australia, which barred under-16s from leading social media platforms in December last year. Indonesia and Malaysia have introduced restrictions for under-16s on certain platforms, while the UK is preparing toblock leading apps for the same age group next year.1:40‘Growing up too young’: Londoners praise under-16s social media ban – videoIn Australia, the affected platforms are Facebook, Instagram, Kick, Reddit, Snapchat, Threads, TikTok, Twitch, X and YouTube.The EU has also said it plans to seek stronger protections for children from harmful social media features, building on the digital services act that already sets rules for tech platforms.Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission, said last month that “it is clear we need age-appropriate restrictions to platforms”. She did not refer to a specific age limit, instead raising the prospect of “phased and gradual access for different age ranges”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThis is EuropeThe most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environmentEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSocial media companies generally oppose blanket bans, arguing that they already have measures to protect younger users, including a minimum age of 13. They ⁠have also said they would comply with government restrictions.Macron, who in April ​urged teenagers to turn off their devices and read in order to become better ​citizens, has asked the French prime ‌minister, Sébastien Lecornu, to ​rework the legislation to address the constitutional council’s concerns, according to the Élysée.The Élysée said Macron remained determined for the reform to take effect before spring 2027, whenFrance holds its presidential election. Macron is ineligible to stand for a third term.Explore more on these topicsSocial media bansFranceEmmanuel MacronSocial mediaDigital mediaEuropean CommissionEuropean UnionnewsShareReuse this content

title: A Queensland man enjoyed soaring profits from a crypto trading app. Then his money started disappearing | Scams | The Guardian
description: The administrative work required to run an effective investment scam has been drastically cut by using merging technology
Author: Ima Caldwell
Headline: The administrative work required to run an effective investment scam has been drastically cut by using merging technology
Content: One Queensland man lost more than $166,000 to an investment scam constructed by AI.Photograph: Thomas Trutschel/Photothek/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenOne Queensland man lost more than $166,000 to an investment scam constructed by AI.Photograph: Thomas Trutschel/Photothek/Getty ImagesScamsA Queensland man enjoyed soaring profits from a crypto trading app. Then his money started disappearingThe administrative work required to run an effective investment scam has been drastically cut by using merging technologyGet ourbreaking news email,free appordaily news podcastIma CaldwellFri 14 Aug 2026 11.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWithin days of clicking on an online ad for a cryptocurrency trading app, a 29-year-old Queensland man watched his dashboard soar with profits.Making investment gains was as simple as downloading the slick-looking app and browser extension linked to his crypto wallet. So he invested more.Then the losses began. Unauthorised transfers started flowing from his crypto wallet and soon he had lost more than $166,000.Frantic, he attempted to contact customer support, only to find the platform’s customer service team was a basic chatbot.It was only then he realised he had fallen victim to an investment scamconstructed by artificial intelligence.‘Scam ecosystems’Data fromScamwatchshows Australians have lost more than $45m to fraudulent investment schemes in 2026 so far, after over $160m in reported losses in 2025.Experts say AI is significantly cutting the administrative work required to run an effective investment scam, replacing cold calls and isolated phishing emails with entire “scam ecosystems”.Dr Marco Navone, an associate professor of finance at the University of Technology Sydney says traditional red flags no longer apply, meaning consumer can’t always recognise the “industrial-grade” deception.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email“Criminal networks can now deploy hyper-realistic, localised media, fake news articles, synthetic reviews … at scale,” Navone says. “[Historically], your first suspicion came from a cheap webpage, or a company phone number that was a mobile number instead of a 1300.“All these small inconsistencies are now gone … this is especially the case when scammers target vulnerable parts of the population.”The Australian Federal Police say scammers can clone voices from a few seconds of audio, generate convincing deepfakes and send thousands of personalised messages based on a victim’s location and online history. AI-generated investment scams often offer access to a “financial adviser” with an Australian or English accent.Regulators can’t keep upWhile the Australian Securities and Investments Commission deactivated nearly 12,000 scam websites in 2025, scammers frequently bypass removal using “cloaking” technology to serve scams to targeted users while showing harmless content to moderators.Cybercrime groups now integrate AI into almost every operational phase, says Dr Andrew Childs, a criminology lecturer at Griffith University.“Offenders can construct an entire environment where each element verifies another,” he says.Digital platforms share responsibility, he says: “In these situations platforms aren’t being passive hosts.“They are actively recommending and distributing advertisements to audiences identified as likely to engage with them.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |When neededSign up toBreaking News AustraliaGet the most important news as it breaksEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNavone says digital platforms should be held legally responsible and be mandated to verify Australian Financial Services (AFS) licensing before publishing investment ads.A 2026 report by the Australian Institute of criminology found that more than 49% of Australians worry about becoming victims of AI-related crime, with 43% identifying AI impersonation as a direct threat.Shifting defence to the financial systemAn AFP spokesperson acknowledged that fund recovery rates remain “incredibly low”, referring to a national scams prevention framework being developed. It will require banks, telecommunications providers and digital platforms to bolster AI scam detection.Experts are calling for more money monitoring, including mandatory confirmation-of-payee systems, forced settlement delays on high-risk transfers and stricter oversight of physical cryptocurrency ATMs.Navone says AI itself becomes a target for social engineering.“Over the coming years, we expect consumers and institutions to increasingly delegate financial decisions, portfolio management and trade execution to autonomous AI agents,” he says. “This introduces a dangerous new frontier: AI tools themselves becoming the targets of social engineering and financial scams.”How to spot an AI-generated investment scamAlways check that an investment provider holds an active AFS licence on theAsic register.If contacted about transferring funds, even by someone you know, call them back directly on the phone number you have for them.Navigate to investment platforms using an independent web search rather than clicking links in ads or messages. You should also check if there are any scam warnings in the search results.If compromised, freeze your bank accounts immediately, change all your passwords, and report it toScamwatchandpolice. Victims can contactIDCAREfor free national identity and cybercrime support.Explore more on these topicsScamsAI (artificial intelligence)Crime - AustraliaCryptocurrenciesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Pocock and crossbenchers call Labor’s NDIS overhaul ‘too far, too fast’ in scathing Senate inquiry report | National disability insurance scheme | The Guardian
description: Greens say Labor’s reform set to ‘rip life-changing supports away from disabled people instead of raising additional revenue through taxing gas exports’
Author: Sarah Basford Canales
Headline: Greens say Labor’s reform set to ‘rip life-changing supports away from disabled people instead of raising additional revenue through taxing gas exports’
Content: Independent senator David Pocock said no participant should be removed from the NDIS until new programs are ‘funded, operating and accessible’.Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAPView image in fullscreenIndependent senator David Pocock said no participant should be removed from the NDIS until new programs are ‘funded, operating and accessible’.Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAPNational disability insurance schemePocock and crossbenchers call Labor’s NDIS overhaul ‘too far, too fast’ in scathing Senate inquiry reportGreens say Labor’s reform set to ‘rip life-changing supports away from disabled people instead of raising additional revenue through taxing gas exports’Sarah Basford CanalesFri 14 Aug 2026 04.04 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 19.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCross-benchers have slammed the Albanese government’s proposed overhaul of the NDIS as going “too far, too fast” as the changes to curb the growth of the $52bn program appear set to pass the parliament as early as next week.The Greens and independent ACT senator,David Pocock, delivered scathing assessments of the bill they warn will enable blunt and indiscriminate cuts to individual budgets supporting more than 770,000 Australians with disabilities in a final Senate inquiry report released on Friday afternoon.The NDIS has given Joe vital social skills. Funding cuts leave his mother fearing how he will ‘do life’Read moreWhile the Labor-chaired committee recommended the bill pass, Greens senator Jordon Steele-John said the proposals would be “devastating to the lives of disabled people and their families”.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailThe bill forms part of the government’s plan to get the NDIS “back on track” and save $37.8bn over four years by tightening the eligibility criteria and subjecting all participants to independent functional assessments from 2028.It will also give the NDIS minister, Mark Butler, the power to reducefunding categories for individualsby up to 99%. The government has already said it will apply a 50% reduction in individual participant budgets for social, civic and community participation.Without the interventions, the government estimates the $52bn-a-year scheme will more than double in cost to $117bn a year in a decade’s time.The Greens have acknowledged some changes should be made to make the NDIS work better for participants but suggested the scheme could be funded by a gas export tax.“The choice that this Labor government is making is to rip life-changing supports away from disabled people instead of raising additional revenue through taxing gas exports shows their priorities clearly,” Steele-John wrote.“This government is choosing the profits of large corporations over the lives of disabled people.”Guardian Australia has previously reported that 241,000 NDIS participantswill be shifted off the scheme by June 2031after the introduction of the functional capacity test, to keep the number of participants at about 600,000.During that period, an additional 105,000 will be stopped from entering the scheme.Those shifted from the scheme are expected to be supported by programs run by states and territories with joint funding from the Commonwealth.Pocock said no participant should be removed from the NDIS until those new programs are “funded, operating and accessible”, vowing to continue scrutiny of the changes.“The true measure of these changes will be found in the experiences of people with disability. They must remain at the centre of what comes next,” Pocock said.Coalition senators provided additional comments raising concerns that fraud and integrity within the NDIS had not been sufficiently addressed.The government is expected to land a deal with the opposition early next week in order to pass the bill in the Senate.Disability advocacy groups have been extremely critical of the government’s amendments to the NDIS, and have warned caring responsibilities will be shifted from the scheme to families, affecting women disproportionately.Women With Disabilities Australia’s chief executive, Sophie Cusworth, said the government should deliver a comprehensive gender impact assessment of the bill.“You cannot say you are working for women while looking to pass legislation that puts women’s safety, care, health and economic security at risk,” she said on Friday.“That is not gender equality. That is neglect.”Explore more on these topicsNational disability insurance schemeMark ButlerDavid PocockAustralian politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lending to property investors falls sharply in ‘tiny’ step towards fairer housing market in Australia, expert says | Housing | The Guardian
description: ABS data shows an almost 9% slump in new lending to investors after three interest rate hikes this year
Author: Cait Kelly
Headline: ABS data shows an almost 9% slump in new lending to investors after three interest rate hikes this year
Content: The latest housing loan data shows investment in existing Australian housing is dropping in favour of new buildings.Photograph: Jono Searle/AAPView image in fullscreenThe latest housing loan data shows investment in existing Australian housing is dropping in favour of new buildings.Photograph: Jono Searle/AAPHousingLending to property investors falls sharply in ‘tiny’ step towards fairer housing market in Australia, expert saysABS data shows an almost 9% slump in new lending to investors after three interest rate hikes this yearFollow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet ourbreaking news email,free appordaily news podcastCait KellyFri 14 Aug 2026 04.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIn what one economist is describing as a “tiny step” toward afairer housing marketafter decades of bad policy, property investors are shying away from established homes, and putting money into new builds instead, new data shows.New lending to property investors fell sharply in the three months to June, slumping almost 9%, ABS data showed, while the number of total new home loans dropped by 5.4% in the June quarter.The major banks have all reported a slump in mortgage applications in recent months,after three RBA official rate hikesand the federal budget’s investor tax changes that together haveweighed on property prices.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailThe ABS’s head of finance statistics, Mish Tan, said: “lending fell across all borrower types this quarter and returned to similar levels to this time last year”.Investor loans led the decline, falling by 8.6% in the June quarter after a 4.7% drop in the previous period. The number of investor loans was 2.8% higher than a year earlier, while the value of loans to investors was down by 10.2%.The number of loans to first home buyers dropped by 2.9% over the three-month period, to be flat over the year.Saul Eslake, a leading housing economist said the interest rates increases this year would be reducing the number of first home buyers..Australia’s falling house prices have a silver lining for mortgage holders. Here’s whyRead more“I don’t think it’s a cause for concern,” he said. “Whereas I would say the big fall in lending to investors for the purchase of established homes is actually something to be welcomed and celebrated.“Because it means that prospective first home buyers are facing less competition from investors motivated by tax breaks for the housing we’ve already got.”The number of loans to investors in established properties was down 14.8%, but the number of loans to investors buying new builds was up by 4.4% to a record high, a possible effect of the government’s budget carve-out for investor lending to build new housing.Eslake said more investment in new builds actually increased rental supply, rather than pitting renters against investors for established housing.He said these stats were a “tiny step” in the right direction to make Australia’s housing market more equal.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |When neededSign up toBreaking News AustraliaGet the most important news as it breaksEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIsn’t it amazing what a policy that actually tackles the cause of outrageous house prices can do? | GrogonomicsRead more“A tiny step. But at least it is in that direction, whereas we’ve been taking tens of thousands of steps in the wrong direction for the last thirty years.”National spokesperson for Everybody’s Home, Maiy Azize, said the figures show the governments tax reforms were “beginning to rebalance the market”.“The most encouraging sign is that investors are pulling back from existing homes while investment in new housing is growing. That means less competition for first home buyers trying to buy a home,” Azize said.“It also smashes the myth that immigration is the main driver of house prices. When governments change the rules and stop boosting investors, housing costs go down.“Housing becoming more affordable is a good thing, especially for people trying to buy their first home.”Explore more on these topicsHousingInterest ratesAustralian economyBankingnewsShareReuse this content

title: BBC seeks to subpoena Trump children and son-in-law over defamation lawsuit | BBC | The Guardian
description: Network wants to serve Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr after president sues over January 6 documentary
Author: Gaya Gupta
Headline: Network wants to serve Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr after president sues over January 6 documentary
Content: From left, Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr at the inauguration of Donald Trump in Washington DC on 20 January 2025.Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/EPAView image in fullscreenFrom left, Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr at the inauguration of Donald Trump in Washington DC on 20 January 2025.Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/EPABBCBBC seeks to subpoena Trump children and son-in-law over defamation lawsuitNetwork wants to serve Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr after president sues over January 6 documentaryGaya GuptaFri 14 Aug 2026 17.05 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 17.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe BBC is trying to subpoena Donald Trump’s children as it builds its defense against the president’s defamation lawsuit centered on a documentary on the January 6 insurrection.In a motion filed on Friday, the BBC sought authorization to serve Trump’s two eldest children,Donald Trump Jrand Ivanka Trump, and son-in-law Jared Kushner, with subpoenas for testimony and their records on the events of 6 January 2021.TheBBC, its lawyers wrote in court documents, is entitled to discover Trump’s “intention behind the speech and anything that bears on the impression his audience could have reasonably obtained in listening to the speech”, which includes whether Trump “gave it intentionally or otherwise; the breadth of the audience of the message and impression; and the extent of any resulting injury or harm”.Trump filed the lawsuit against the BBC in December over scenes in the 2024 BBC documentary Trump, A Second Chance?. It argued that the BBC spliced scenes from Trump’s 6 January 2021 speech so that it appeared Trump directly urged his supporters to attack the US Capitol building.Trump’s children and son-in-law have, “without question”, knowledge of several incidents that day, BBC’s lawyers wrote, , including when Trump sought to convince former vice-president Mike Pence to refuse certifying the results of the 2020 election. The BBC also said that Kushner allegedly helped to draft a statement for Trump that would have condemned the use of violence at the Capitol.The British broadcaster had been unable to previously serve Trump’s children and son-in-law with subpoenas because they are protected by the US Secret Service as members of the sitting president’s immediate family, according to the court documents. The BBC had tried previously to serveIvanka Trumpand her husband, Kushner, at their home in Florida but were blocked by law enforcement officials.Trump’s legal team did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Last week, a federal judge granted Trump’s request to block the BBC from accessingfinancial recordsafter Trump’s lawyers said they would amend the lawsuit to focus specifically on the reputational damages rather than business impacts. Another judge had previously ruled that Trump would have to start handing over records that would have provided details on the hundreds of businesses owned by Trump’s family trust.Trump recentlyclaimedthat the BBC used artificial intelligence to alter his speech, which the network has denied. While the BBC has apologized for the editing, it has maintained that Trump lacks the grounds for a defamation lawsuit.The BBC is being represented by the law firm Ballard Spahr, which has also defended several publications facing lawsuits from Trump and his allies, including the New York Times and the Associated Press. It is one of several media organizations that Trump has targeted after they published critical reporting of him. The Wall Street Journal is also facing a $10bn lawsuit for its reporting on Trump’s alleged contributions to Jeffrey Epstein’s birthday book, and several journalists at the New York Times were subpoenaed over an article detailing security concerns with the Air Force One presidential jet.Explore more on these topicsBBCDonald TrumpUS Capitol attackDocumentary filmsEuropeJared KushnerIvanka TrumpnewsShareReuse this content

title: Hundreds arrested on suspicion of arson in France as wildfires rage across Europe | France | The Guardian
description: One person killed and hundreds evacuated in Croatia as blazes also hit Germany, Greece and Spain
Author: Jon Henley
Headline: One person killed and hundreds evacuated in Croatia as blazes also hit Germany, Greece and Spain
Content: A wildfire burns near Omiš, Croatia.Photograph: Jakov Prkic/CROPIX/SIPA/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenA wildfire burns near Omiš, Croatia.Photograph: Jakov Prkic/CROPIX/SIPA/ShutterstockFranceHundreds arrested on suspicion of arson in France as wildfires rage across EuropeOne person killed and hundreds evacuated in Croatia as blazes also hit Germany, Greece and SpainJon Henleyin ParisFri 14 Aug 2026 12.58 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 08.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlmost 500 people have been arrested on suspicion of starting wildfires in France since the start of the summer, authorities have said, as firefighters in half a dozen European countries tackle ferocious blazes amid a record-breaking heatwave.A fire engulfed ⁠homes in a Croatian holiday resort on Friday, killing one person, injuring 40 and forcing 1,200 to evacuate, officials said, as the EU warned that pockets of “very extreme” wildfire conditions stretched across the continent.Europe is the world’s fastest warming continent. What is to blame?Read moreHundreds more people were evacuated from villages in westernGermanyand south-west France, while stranded holidaymakers were picked up from beaches threatened by flames in Greece, and the army rescued historic relics in Spain.With three in five Europeans facing temperatures of at least 30C on Friday and about 150 million enduring 35C or more, France’s interior ministry said 474 people, including 183 minors, had been detained over wildfires in the country since 1 July.About 70% of those arrested were suspected of deliberately starting fires and the rest of doing so accidentally. French media said a 15-year-old boy had been detained in connection with a fire near Bordeaux airport that killed two firefighters in July.French authorities on Friday evacuated more than 525 people from the village of Luglon in the south-west region of Landes after a new wildfire tore through almost 1,100 hectares (2,700 acres) of tinder-dry pine forest in less than 24 hours.“The situation is unfavourable and the fire remains raging,” Gilles Clavreul, a regional official, told reporters, ​adding that 500 firefighters were tackling ‌the flames and six water-dumping aircraft ‌had been sent to assist. Roads to the village were closed.View image in fullscreenA firefighter with the French air force looks on as a wildfire burns through the Landes forest in Luglon, south-west France.Photograph: Romain Perrocheau/AFP/Getty ImagesLuglon is about 62 miles (100km) south-east of the popular holiday destinations of Arcachon Bay and the Lège-Cap-Ferret peninsula wheretwo huge wildfiresdestroyed more than 50,000 hectares in late July,forcing the evacuation of as many as 220,000 people.Scientists say climate breakdown is causing more frequent and more extreme weather events,evaporating soilsand waterways, fuelling wildfires and leading tothousands of excess deathsin France. Europe isheating at about twice the globalaverage rate.The EU’s Copernicus climate change service warned in its weekly outlook of “very extreme” conditions across a ​large area of central and eastern Europe, with other pockets over southern Britain, Ireland, northern France and southern Sweden.The average high across western Europe on ‌Friday was forecast to be 31.2C, which is 8C above what was typical from 1961 to 1990, data from the Reuters Climate Monitor showed. The temperature for Europe as a whole was 1.6C above the 1961-1990 norm.In western Germany, more than 2,000 people fled their homes early on Friday morning to take shelter in a nearby primary school after a ⁠wildfire in the nearby Hürtgen forest spread to within a few hundred metres of the village of Gey.“This forest fire threatens to hit the local ‌community hard,” Mona Neubaur, the deputy premier of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, posted on social media. Unexploded second world war ordnance was also hampering firefighting efforts.View image in fullscreenA police helicopter carries water to be dumped on ⁠wildfire in the Hürtgen forest in western Germany.Photograph: Roberto Pfeil/afp/AFP/Getty ImagesThe news agency dpa reported explosions could be heard as munitions detonated in the flames, forcing firefighters to stay out of the area, not far from the Belgian border, for safety. German army tanks and helicopters were providing support.In Croatia, a wildfire driven by strong winds descended on the tourist town of Lokva Rogoznica on the Dalmatian coast overnight. Police said they had located the body of one person while searching burned areas on Friday afternoon.Emergency ​shelters opened in several nearby towns. Of 36 people treated by ambulance services in the city of Split, about 15.5 miles to the north, 14 were admitted to hospital and seven had life-threatening injuries, local health officials said.View image in fullscreenCroatia’s prime minister described the blaze that spread to Omiš as ‘one of the worst fires in recent years’.Photograph: Tom Dubravec/AP“It was a strong fire, it swept everything on ‌its way ... there has been huge material damage,” Slavko Tucaković, the regional chief fire commander, said on Friday, adding that the blaze appeared to have calmed by Friday morning.The country’s prime minister, Andrej ‌Plenković, said on a visit to nearby Omiš, where the evacuees were sheltering in a sports hall, that the blaze was “one of the worst fires in recent years” but “most importantly” there were no confirmed fatalities so far.View image in fullscreenA painting is removed as a wildfire nears the San Juan de la Peña monastery in Aragón, north-east Spain.Photograph: UME/AFP/Getty ImagesIn north-eastSpain, an army unit removed the remains of three 11th-century Aragonese kings from the San Juan de la Peña monastery after it was threatened by a wildfire and took them to a ​museum in nearby Huesca.The fire, which began on Monday, intensified on ⁠Thursday, authorities said, driven by higher temperatures and strong winds that have enabled it burn through more ​than 9,000 hectares, forcing ​the evacuation of 16 towns and villages.View image in fullscreenLocal residents and tourists are evacuated from Siviri as a forest fire threatens the resort on Halkidiki peninsula, Greece.Photograph: Alexandros Avramidis/ReutersA ​much larger wildfire in southern Spain also worsened on Thursday. It has so far burned 31,000 hectares in the province of Huelva and forced the evacuation of about 700 people.In northern Greece, a fleet ofsmall boats evacuated about 500 holidaymakersfrom beaches on Thursday as a forest fire threatened Siviri and Fourka, two popular resorts on the Halkidiki peninsula, south of the city of Thessaloniki.The 2-mile-long fire front, with flames up to 30 metres (98ft) high, was brought under control later in the day, the regional civil protection chief said, though crews remained on alert for flare-ups. Two injured firefighters were taken to hospital, the fire service added.View image in fullscreenThe remains of homes in Stoke-on-Trent smoulder on Friday as wildfire raced across the West MidlandsPhotograph: Christopher Furlong/Getty ImagesA maximum level-five alert for fires was issued for much of the Greek mainland and local officials in Halkidiki have banned access to the region’s dense pine forests. Winds of up to 62 mph are forecast for Friday.In the UK,wildfires raced across the West Midlands, burning several houses to the ground in “one of the most significant” incidents the region’s fire service has ever had to deal with, the regional fire chief, Simon Tuhill, said.Reuters and Agence-France Press contributed to this reportExplore more on these topicsFranceWildfiresGermanySpainCroatiaGreeceEnglandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Belgian student strikes gold worth €9m while digging a new sewer | Belgium | The Guardian
description: Kobe, 18, who made discovery on site of former brewery in Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde, at first thought trove was €1 coins
Author: Jon Henley
Headline: Kobe, 18, who made discovery on site of former brewery in Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde, at first thought trove was €1 coins
Content: Kobe said the gold was ‘really bricked in there – not in a safe or anything’.Photograph: Gianni Barbieux/Photo NewsView image in fullscreenKobe said the gold was ‘really bricked in there – not in a safe or anything’.Photograph: Gianni Barbieux/Photo NewsBelgiumBelgian student strikes gold worth €9m while digging a new sewerKobe, 18, who made discovery on site of former brewery in Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde, at first thought trove was €1 coinsJon HenleyEurope correspondentFri 14 Aug 2026 11.52 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 12.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor a student with a summer job working on a Belgian building site, “money down the drain” has taken on a whole new meaning: excavating the trenches for a sewage system, he stumbled across a hidden trove of gold worth an estimated €9m (£8m).“We suddenly saw something lying there,” 18-year-old Kobetold the Belgian news network VTM. “At first I thought it was €1 coins. So we started digging them up. Then we saw a gold bar. It turned out to be a bit more than we thought.”The student, who has not been further identified, was working with colleagues on the site of a former brewery on Van Langenhovestraat in Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde, about 19 miles (30km) north-west of Brussels, when they made the discovery on Tuesday.View image in fullscreenThe hoard was stashed in a bag in a bricked-in cellar wall beneath the grand villa.Photograph: Facebook/Dendermonde Local PoliceThe hoard, which includes gold coins, nuggets and numbered bullion bars, was stashed in a bag in a bricked-in cellar wall beneath the grand villa originally built for the brewery’s owner, Theophilus Van Assche, in the late 19th century.Kobe said: “It’s just not something you expect when you’re working on a regular Tuesday morning,” adding that the treasure trove appeared to have been deliberately hidden. “It was really bricked in there – not in a safe or anything.”Brewing on the site began in 1899 and ceased in 1970, and the listed property – the wrought-iron gates of which still bear the initials “VA” – is being completely renovated by the social welfare organisation CAW Oost-Vlaanderen to create new offices and housing.View image in fullscreenThe trove included gold coins, nuggets and numbered bullion bars.Photograph: Facebook/Dendermonde Local Police“The Brouwershuis was a beautiful building, but it is being completely gutted,” Geert Hillaert, of CAW,told the news outlet HLN. “Ultimately, only the walls will remain. Labourers were laying drainage pipes when they stumbled across the gold.”Kobe and his colleagues called the police and notified CAW as soon as they came across the gold hoard. The treasure has since been transferred to a secure facility in Brussels pending a detailed official investigation to establish its legal ownership.Hanne Ollevier, of the East Flanders public prosecutor’s office, told HLN that authorities must first verify that the bullion was not stolen property or the proceeds of criminal activity, and was likely to spark a complex civil dispute.View image in fullscreenBelgian law requires finders to wait at least five years for potential owners to claim any treasure.Photograph: Facebook/Dendermonde Local PoliceThe building contractors, the welfare organisation and any descendants of the once-wealthy Van Assche family could all have a claim to part of the fortune. Belgian law requires finders to wait at least five years for potential owners to claim any treasure.A former mayor of Dendermonde,Piet Buyse, told HLNthat the Van Assche’s fortune had “certainly stayed in the family. It wouldn’t surprise me at all if they had decided to put at least some of it in gold, and then to hide it in a safe place.”For his part, Kobe said he and his colleagues had understood straight away that they had to hand over such a big find. “If it had been a few coins, maybe not,” he said. “But maybe we’ll get some kind of finder’s reward eventually.”Explore more on these topicsBelgiumEuropenewsShareReuse this content

title: Iberian orca known for ramming boats seen with suspected gunshot wounds | Whales | The Guardian
description: Marine conservationist says deliberate attack would be ‘act of extreme cruelty’ against endangered population
Author: Ashifa Kassam
Headline: Marine conservationist says deliberate attack would be ‘act of extreme cruelty’ against endangered population
Content: Toñi, the oldest orca in her pod, has been seen with markings on her dorsal fin that suggest pellet gun fire.Photograph: Cristina Otero Sabio/WeWhale.org and Iberian Orcas GuardiansView image in fullscreenToñi, the oldest orca in her pod, has been seen with markings on her dorsal fin that suggest pellet gun fire.Photograph: Cristina Otero Sabio/WeWhale.org and Iberian Orcas GuardiansWhalesIberian orca known for ramming boats seen with suspected gunshot woundsMarine conservationist says deliberate attack would be ‘act of extreme cruelty’ against endangered populationAshifa Kassamin MadridFri 14 Aug 2026 11.07 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 10.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSpanish officials have launched an investigation after the matriarch of an orca pod known for jostling and ramming boats off the Iberian Peninsula was spotted with wounds suggesting she had been shot by a pellet gun.On Friday, Spain’s environment ministry said Toñi, the oldest living member of the pod,had been seen swimmingin the Strait of Gibraltar with markings on her dorsal fin that were “consistent with shots from a pellet gun”.Humpbacks return to Rio: the whales are back from the brink of extinction – but will tourism help or hinder?Read moreA source from the ministrytold El Paísthat some of the projectiles remained lodged in her fin, posing a risk of infection. The ministry was in touch with officials in Portugal, the source added, as the markings were detected after the orcas had travelled from the waters off the Portuguese city of Faro.The orcas of the Iberian Peninsulaburst into headlinesin 2020 after sailors shared stories of rudders that had been rammed and boats that had been spun 180 degrees or tipped sideways. Since then, a small group of orcas from the pod have been blamed for damaging scores of vessels and sinking at least four boats, leaving scientists scrambling to explain the baffling behaviour.Scientists have long pushed back against the assertion that the orcas are attacking vessels, instead suggesting that the behaviour could be a form of play or a means of practising their hunting skills.In the days since Toñi’s injuries came to light, the WeWhale and Iberian Orca Guardians (IOG) association have been closely tracking the animal for any sign of weakness. “We know Toñi. We were with her a few weeks ago and these wounds were not there,” the IOG co-founder Janek Andre said.“Seeing Toñi,laabuela[the grandmother], like this is devastating,” he added. “If someone has deliberately fired a shotgun at her, this is not only an act of extreme cruelty against an individual animal. It is an attack on one of the last remaining members of a critically endangered population.”Researchers have long sought to highlight the many stressors faced by this population of orcas as they navigate life in a major shipping route. Food scarcity, injuries and pollution have left the population on a knife’s edge, reduced to between 30 and 40 individuals.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toDown to EarthThe planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essentialEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn 2023, video emerged thatappeared to show people launchingfirecrackers into the sea as orcas rammed the rudder of their vessel, hinting that the animals were now facing another threat as sailors push back against their actions.“There has been enormous public discussion about Iberian orcas and their interactions with vessels,” said Andre. “Whatever someone’s opinion about those interactions may be, shooting at these animals can never be an acceptable response. These orcas need protection, not retaliation.”Explore more on these topicsWhalesSpainEuropeCetaceansMarine lifeWildlifenewsShareReuse this content

title: Trump threatens to declare strait of Hormuz ‘territory of the United States’ | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: Seriousness of remark made in New York on Friday, and whether it signaled new policy ​position, not clear
Author: Maya Yang
Headline: Seriousness of remark made in New York on Friday, and whether it signaled new policy ​position, not clear
Content: Donald Trump at the David S Mack Center for Training and Intelligence in Garden City, New York, on Friday.Photograph: Samuel Corum/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDonald Trump at the David S Mack Center for Training and Intelligence in Garden City, New York, on Friday.Photograph: Samuel Corum/Getty ImagesDonald TrumpTrump threatens to declare strait of Hormuz ‘territory of the United States’Seriousness of remark made in New York on Friday, and whether it signaled new policy ​position, not clearMaya YangFri 14 Aug 2026 17.38 EDTFirst published on Fri 14 Aug 2026 17.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trumphas threatened to declare the strait of Hormuz as “a territory of the United States” as his administration struggles to conclude the war with Iran.During a speech at a police academy on Long Island, New York, on Friday, the US president said he would “pretty soon” designate the waterway – a crucial chokepoint for global trade, through which about a fifth of the world’s seaborne oil supplies typically pass – a US territory.The comment came as peace talks withIranremain at an impasse following failed negotiations, with Tehran refusing to reopen the strait, which has been all but closed since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February.Almost six months into the war, there is little indication that negotiations will soon yield peace, as Iranian officials continue to defy Trump’s demands. The US has been blockading Iranian shipping and ⁠ports in recent months in an effort to pile economic pressure on Tehran.“After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz strait a territory of the United States,” Trump said on Friday. “Essentially, that’s what it is. We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to.”The seriousness of Trump’s remark, and whether it signaled a new policy ​position for his administration, was not immediately clear.Responding on X, formerly Twitter, Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister, said Tehran would not ⁠be intimidated by threats, ​or ‌a show ‌of force, by ‌the US – and added that the strait of Hormuz ​would only ​be opened, ​or ‌closed, under Iran’s ​authority.Earlier this week, the president claimed that the US had “total control” over the strait and said “I think we will keep it” on Truth Social, despite the waterway being an internationally navigable strait bordered by Iran and Oman.Fuel prices have risen sharplysince the start of the war, forcing working Americans to pay significantly more at the pump.Nevertheless, on Friday, Trump said that Americans who have had to “pay a tiny little bit more for your gasoline” should remember that they are “doing it so that a very evil country cannot have a – really, it’s the No 1 state sponsor of terror in the world – we don’t want them to have a nuclear weapon.“When you have to pay a little bit more, you’re at $4, it’s OK, I mean, it’s not. I’ll never apologize. I did the right thing,” he added.Over the past six months, the Trump administration hasrepeatedly claimed victoryin the war, saying Iran’s regime has been pleading for a deal.Tehran has remained steadfast in its demands,sayingas recently as last Saturday that it will not reopen the strait of Hormuz unless the US “corrects its behavior”, “completely compensate[s]” Iran for war damage, lifts sanctions and “unconditionally” releases frozen assets.Explore more on these topicsDonald TrumpUS-Israel war on IranUS politicsIranStrait of HormuzMiddle East and north AfricanewsShareReuse this content

title: Israeli military plans to transfer law enforcement in occupied West Bank to police | West Bank | The Guardian
description: Palestine’s vice-president calls plan ‘flagrant violation of international law’ and a step towards full Israeli annexation
Author: Emma Graham-Harrison
Headline: Palestine’s vice-president calls plan ‘flagrant violation of international law’ and a step towards full Israeli annexation
Content: Israeli forces preventing Israeli and foreign peace activists from delivering supplies to a besieged Palestinian home.Photograph: Nasser ishatyeh/SOPA Images/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenIsraeli forces preventing Israeli and foreign peace activists from delivering supplies to a besieged Palestinian home.Photograph: Nasser ishatyeh/SOPA Images/ShutterstockWest BankIsraeli military plans to transfer law enforcement in occupied West Bank to policePalestine’s vice-president calls plan ‘flagrant violation of international law’ and a step towards full Israeli annexationEmma Graham-Harrisonin JerusalemFri 14 Aug 2026 13.52 EDTLast modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 14.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIsrael’s defence minister wants to transfer law enforcement powers for Israelis in the occupied West Bank over to the police, a plan that Palestine’s vice-president described as a “flagrant violation of international law” and step towards full Israeli annexation.Israel Katz announced that he had ordered the military to draw up plans for the handover of responsibility for policing Israeli settlers amid domestic and international criticism ofthe army’s failure to tackle militants besieging three Palestinian families.The Palestinian vice-president, Hussein al-Sheikh, called for international intervention to enforce international law and stop a move that would “entrench the illegitimate annexation of Palestinian land”.Katz unveiled his plan as a settler siege in the Palestinian village of Qusra entered its sixth day. The Israeli army has proved unable or unwilling to removethe group of militants trying to drive out Palestinian residentsthrough a campaign of terror.View image in fullscreenIsraeli soldiers watch Israeli settlers setting up a tent just outside the entrance of a besieged Palestinian family home in the village of Qusra, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on 14 August 2026.Photograph: Jaafar Ashtiyeh/AFP/Getty ImagesMichael Sfard, a leading Israeli human rights lawyer, said a transfer of law enforcement powers could constitute a major step towards formal annexation.“The military can delegate enforcement but not responsibility [of the law],” Sfard said. “If they want to create a normative legal framework that absolves the army from responsibility and transfers it to police, that would be another brick, a very major one, of annexation.”However, Israel could also legally expand police powers in the occupiedWest Bankunder the current occupation framework, he added, and the lack of detail in Katz’s statement indicated it may have been driven more by politics than clear policy.“This is a cowardly statement made by a minister of defence who is under scrutiny, because the army that reached Syria, Iran and Lebanon and annihilated Gaza cannot evacuate a few Jewish terrorists that invaded a Palestinian home in an area under occupation for six decades.”View image in fullscreenPalestinian, Israeli and foreign activists attempt to deliver basic supplies to three Palestinian families under siege by settlers in Qusra.Photograph: Anadolu/Getty ImagesThere has been a surge in attacks on Palestiniansand construction of new settlements across the occupied West Bank, as extremists backed by the most far-right government in Israel’s history intensify a campaign of ethnic cleansing ahead ofnational elections set for October.On Thursday Katz celebrated the re-establishment of a settlement evacuated by Israel in 2005, under then-prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan.“Here, this is the land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Katz said at the ceremony in Ganim, where two dozen prefabricated homes have already been installed, and the hillside is being levelled to make space for more.On the road that leads to the settlement the army had levelled Palestinian property and used piles of rubble to block access roads for Palestinian communities.On Friday the commander of Israeli forces for the occupied West Bank, Gen Avi Bluth, made a second visit to Qusra.
